newsitem.title: UK: Med and UKC tanker activity picks up, rates lift.
newsitem.headline: Med and UKC tanker activity picks up, rates lift.

text.p: Crude tanker fixing in the Mediterranean/Black Sea and UK-Continent sectors quickened on Thursday. European shipping brokers said rates were stronger in both sectors.
Repsol's chartering of a Nissos TBN travelling Med-Spain at W102.5 carrying 80,000 tonnes was seen as typical of the market, Italian brokers said.
"Activity has been better today, with rates strengthening. Vessels have been leaving this area, so that essentially accounts for the rates rise," a broker said.
Suezmaxes were seen to have settled at last done levels of W72 for cross Med trips.
Tanker fixing in the UKC sector improved substantially, with at least four Aframaxes finding employment on cross-UKC trips.
Brokers said Petrofina's chartering of the Katja, travelling Tees-Immmingham at W107.5, reflected the market, though as low as W97.5 was seen done.
Four transatlantic trips were seen with an Aframax finding employment to the USAC, a Suezmax to east coast Canada, and two VLCCs fixed by Statoil travelling to U.S. Gulf and E.C. Canada.
It was rumoured that a trader was in possession of three North Sea cargoes and was considering taking a fourth and making up a VLCC. It was unclear where the cargoes were headed.
Tanker fixing in the all important Middle East market was good on Thursday and rates were seen to be slightly stronger on two of the three routes out of the region.
Tankers making trips to Japan had crept up to W57.5, with rates for Eastern voyages placed at W55, up W2 points. VLCCs heading for the West were seen at W50, down W3 points.
Vessels in the Far East/Pacific were being hit by several typhoons -- Yates, Zane and Sally.
